summary: Two panes and a divider between them that a person moves — by dragging, or with the arrow keys — for two views read across, where which one needs the room depends on the reader.
useWhen: two views of one thing are read across and both have long lines — a request and its response, a source and its preview, a log and its detail
the right split depends on the content and on the reader, so it is theirs to set

useInstead.when: detail that opens beside a list when something is picked, and closes
useInstead.why: a SidePanel, in SidePanelLayout, is a region that comes and goes, with a title, a close button and a Drawer on a phone; a split is two panes that are always there

useInstead.when: columns that are simply laid out — a main column and an aside
useInstead.why: a layout nobody needs to change should not offer a control that changes it; every divider is one more tab stop

useInstead.when: one table column is too narrow
useInstead.why: its `resize`, from useTableColumns, is the column's own handle in its header; a split around a table resizes the table, not the column

composition.note: `start` and `end` are the panes; `label` names the divider by what it resizes — "Resize the API request". The value is the first pane's share in percent: `defaultSize`, or `size` with `onSizeChange` to keep it (in the browser, say). Bound it with `minSize` and `maxSize`. Side by side it stacks at `collapse` (mobile by default); a vertical split needs a height from its container.
composition.example: <SplitPane label="Resize the API request" defaultSize={55} minSize={30} maxSize={70} collapse="tablet" start={<CodeSnippet type="multi" …>{request}</CodeSnippet>} end={<CodeSnippet type="multi" …>{response}</CodeSnippet>} />

start.note: the first pane — start side, or top — whose share the divider sets; it scrolls on its own

end.note: the second pane, taking the rest; it scrolls on its own

requires: a `label` naming what the divider resizes: it is the control's only name
guarantees: the divider is a focusable `separator` (the ARIA window-splitter pattern) with the first pane's share as `aria-valuenow`, `minSize` and `maxSize` as its bounds, and `aria-controls` pointing at the first pane
the arrow keys along its axis move it 2%, with Shift 10%; Home and End go to the bounds; Enter and a double-click put it back at `defaultSize`
the arrow moves the divider the way it points: side by side in a right-to-left page the first pane is on the right, so → shrinks it
a drag moves it, with the pointer held, and selects no text on the way
each pane scrolls on its own, and its content cannot widen it
at the collapse breakpoint the panes stack and the divider is removed, from the tab order too
a grip at the divider's middle marks it movable at 3:1; focused or dragged, the line and the grip turn to border/focus, and in forced colours to Highlight
notes: The share is percent, not pixels: it survives a window resize, and the value announced means something without knowing the width.
Nothing is kept between visits; keep `size` yourself, from `onSizeChange`, when it should be.

antiPatterns.dont: a SplitPane for a main column and an aside nobody needs to resize
antiPatterns.why: a divider is a control and a tab stop; offered where nothing is gained, it is one more thing to tab past

antiPatterns.dont: a SplitPane whose end pane is a detail that opens and closes
antiPatterns.why: the panel's title, close button and Drawer fallback are SidePanel's; an empty pane behind a divider is a layout with a hole in it
two panes side by side on a phone are two strips too narrow to read
